newsitem.title: UK: Greater derivatives disclosure in draft U.K. rules.
newsitem.headline: Greater derivatives disclosure in draft U.K. rules.

text.p: A wide range of firms in operating in Britain, including all banks and insurance companies, will have to give far more details about their exposure to financial risk through derivatives than hitherto under a draft accounting plan released on Thursday.

Britain's Accounting Standards Board (ASB) said its draft proposals for the disclosure of derivatives and other financial instruments were a significant step forward towards bringing Britain into line with international standards on financial instruments.

"There have in recent years been significant changes in the way in which companies obtain finance and manage the resulting risks. In the UK, accounting practice has struggled to keep up with these changes," ASB technical director Allan Cook said.
The ASB said it had drawn on the work of standard setters in the U.S., Australia, Canada and New Zealand in framing its proposals which were "broadly consistent with international practice".

It said it had sought to reduce the required disclosures to what was essential to provide a broad overview of an entity's financial instruments and its risk position, focusing on those which were of greatest significance.
"The proposed requirements...should meet the reasonable demands of users for more information whilst avoiding the provision of a mass of detailed data that is unlikely to be helpful," Cook added.
Firms covered by the proposals include all entities with a capital instrument listed on a stock exchange or a market in Britain or elsewhere and all banks and insurance companies.
They will be required to provide information about the major financial risks they face in their activities and how they manage their exposure to these risks.
Certain numerical information has to be disclosed including an analysis of a firm's borrowings to show interest rate, currency and maturity profiles.

Firms will also have to give a summary of the fair values of the financial instruments held and a summary of the fair value of financial instruments held for trading purposes along with an analysis of the net gains or losses arising from trading.
They will also have to give details of the effects of the use of hedge accounting techniques on the profit and loss account, the statement of total recognised losses and gains and the balance sheet.
The ASB said contracts for the delivery of gold and certain types of commodity contracts were regarded as financial instruments for the purposes of most of the disclosure requirements.
